headline: Chips slide as Amodei, Altman and Musk call for slowing AI development
summary: After Amodei's Saturday essay warning AI agents could cause hundreds of billions in damage within 6-12 months, backed by Altman (who shelved an OpenAI IPO this year) and Musk, the SOX fell 5.9%, NVDA -3.4%, AMD -4.4%, MU -5.3%, ASML -6% and SoftBank -10%.

headline: 10-year yield touches 5.01%, highest since October 2023, as oil tops $100
summary: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and a strike on the east-west pipeline pushed Brent near $107 and WTI above $102, reviving inflation fears; heavy AI-related corporate debt issuance and fiscal worries added to the move. The 30-year sits at 5.35%.

headline: Goldman previews Micron FQ4 (Sep 30): 'another strong quarter'
summary: Goldman models revenue $51.9B vs $50.4B consensus, EPS $32.54 and 87.3% gross margin on continued supply constraints, but notes DRAM price momentum is now more measured; it holds a $1,100 target vs Street $1,564.

headline: 30-year fixed mortgage hits 7.17%, highest since January 2025
summary: Mortgage News Daily's average rose to a new long-term high ahead of Wednesday's FOMC, where a hike is a live risk; refinance economics are dead at these levels.

headline: GOOGL +3.2% Monday on plans for a New Mexico AI data center
summary: Alphabet closed at $349.39 after announcing an AI data-center build in New Mexico, alongside Waymo opening Las Vegas service and a Tokyo plan for 2027.

headline: HomeSmart taps loanDepot for lending; stock still at $0.83, under NYSE's $1
summary: loanDepot signed a marketing services agreement with HomeSmart, the largest 100%-commission brokerage (~25,000 agents). It does not address the listing problem: LDI closed Monday at $0.8333, four-plus weeks below $1 with no reverse-split announcement.

headline: Anthropic IPO still on for 2026: Nasdaq chosen, Nvidia in talks as anchor investor
summary: Axios reports the IPO remains on track for 2026 despite the safety debate Amodei himself ignited; Reuters reported Nvidia in talks to anchor what could be the largest IPO in history (Sep 11), Business Insider says Nasdaq won the listing (Sep 13), and the timeline has shifted to mid-October. OpenAI, by contrast, shelved its IPO this year.

headline: Amodei, Altman and Musk call for slowing AI development; AI stocks sell off Monday
summary: Anthropic's CEO proposed slowing the pace of capability gains on control-loss and misuse risk, echoed by Altman and Musk; Monday's reaction: NVDA -3.4%, MRVL -7.3%, MU -5.3%, TSM ADR -3.5% while cybersecurity names rallied.

headline: Altman rules out an OpenAI IPO this year
summary: Altman said an IPO now would come at an ill-advised moment given AI safety concerns, calling extinction risk unacceptable; SoftBank's funding support continues with an upsized $11.9B loan reported Sep 14.

headline: August CPI 0.4% m/m, 3.4% y/y; core 0.3% beats forecasts
summary: Gasoline +3.9% on the month drove over a third of the increase (energy +16.3% y/y) and core rose a faster-than-forecast 0.3% m/m. The print locked in Wednesday's hike, with futures moving to ~90% within days.

headline: SK hynix revises wage deal - cash share of bonuses up to 50%, union vote Sep 15-16
summary: The revised offer answers the stock-heavy bonus objection that sank the first deal by 25 votes; members vote company-wide Sep 15-16. With DRAM inventories reported under 10 days and BofA lifting its target to $268, the ADR is +7.7% since Aug 27 despite Monday's 7.6% selloff hit. A yes vote removes the last company-specific gate.

headline: TSMC August revenue a record NT$514.8B, up 53.3%
summary: First month ever above NT$500B and the fourth straight monthly record, confirming AI chip demand ran hot through August; Taipei shares sit ~5% under their all-time high.

headline: Muse AI agent hits No. 2 on the US App Store two days after launch
summary: Meta launched Muse, a personal AI agent that can act across apps (email, payments, travel), on Sep 8; by Sep 10 it ranked No. 2 on iOS despite modest absolute downloads (~83k US iOS). The stock re-rated ~16% over the gap on agent optimism.

headline: Anthropic details Alibaba distillation campaign: 151M Claude exchanges via 3,500 accounts
summary: Anthropic alleges Alibaba harvested Claude's reasoning, coding and agentic outputs at up to ~3M exchanges a day (May-July) to train its own models; Beijing rejected the allegations Sep 12. Adds legal and US-China friction risk while class actions (Oct 5 lead-plaintiff deadline) already circle.

headline: Apple unveils iPhone Duo, its first foldable, at $1,999 - Ternus's first event as CEO
summary: 7.6-inch inner / 5.4-inch outer displays, A20 Pro chip, titanium, preorders Oct 16 and availability Oct 23; iPhone 18 Pro, Watch Series 12 with a new Health Sensing System and AirPods 5 rounded out the event. Some analysts see the Duo reaching 10% of iPhone sales; KeyBanc cautioned on expectations and iPhone 18 delivery lead times are tracking below iPhone 17's. AAPL steady near records, $333.08 on Sep 14.

headline: Qualcomm and Amazon strike multi-generational AI data-center infrastructure deal
summary: Qualcomm announced a multi-generational product collaboration with Amazon to build next-generation AI data-center infrastructure, diversifying AWS's silicon supply beyond Nvidia and its own Trainium line.

headline: Enphase pushes IQ solid-state transformer for AI data centers, built in Texas
summary: Enphase said power modules for its IQ solid-state transformer are now being built in Texas and showcased the product at AI Infra Summit on Sep 14 - a pivot of its power-electronics IP toward data-center demand while residential stays soft.

headline: August payrolls +162k, well above forecasts; unemployment steady at 4.1%
summary: Payrolls rose 162,000 versus a 31,000 average over the prior 12 months, with June and July revised up a combined 55k and wages +0.3% m/m (+3.1% y/y). The reacceleration removed the labour-market case against a hike.

headline: Bloom Energy joins the S&P 500 effective Sep 21
summary: S&P DJI adds Bloom, Illumina and Everpure at the September rebalance. The stock jumped ~11% on inclusion bets and Mizuho raised its target to $351 from $242; BE closed Sep 14 at $257.05, +16% vs Aug 27 - the list's best performer over the gap. Astera Labs, the other rumoured candidate, missed out.

headline: Nvidia confirms $12.9B acquisition of Hugging Face
summary: The previously reported deal is now official, one of Nvidia's largest acquisitions ever, putting the dominant GPU maker in control of the main open-model distribution platform.

headline: Cloudflare partners with OpenAI on AI-driven vulnerability remediation; Cursor agents move onto its Sandboxes
summary: New Vulnerability Discovery and Remediation service built on GPT-5.6 Cyber models (Sep 3), a day after Cursor Cloud Agents began running on Cloudflare Sandboxes; Adaptive Intelligence bot defense launched Aug 31. On Sep 14 NET rose 7.8% to $330.36 - near its 52-week high - as security rallied while AI hardware sold off.

headline: Judge Brinkema spares Google an ad-tech breakup, orders behavioral remedies
summary: The court rejected the DOJ's demand to divest AdX and DFP, instead ordering real-time bid transparency, an end to Unified Pricing Rules and first/last-look privileges. Third straight US structural remedy Google has avoided; the last big domestic overhang is gone.

headline: Broadcom Q3: revenue $29.6B +86%, AI revenue $16.7B +221% - but the Q4 guide was sold
summary: Beat on top and bottom (non-GAAP EPS $3.32, +96%); Q4 guided to ~$34.8B (+93%) with AI ~$21.7B, read as light against buyside hopes - shares fell over 6% after hours and closed Sep 14 at $344.72 (-6% vs Aug 27). Hock Tan on CNBC Sep 14: AI revenue targets haven't changed.

headline: GTA VI preview becomes Netflix's most-watched program at 31.1M views
summary: The 27-minute exclusive ranked #1 in 87 of 93 tracked countries and beat every Netflix original that week; a later report credited it with 100k+ US sign-ups in its six-hour exclusivity window.

headline: Figure completes Kiavi acquisition
summary: Figure closed its acquisition of Kiavi, expanding its blockchain-native capital marketplace; it followed on Sep 10 with a Sierra deal putting AI agents on abandoned home-equity applications. The August slide bottomed at $33.19 on Sep 2.

headline: Credo's record Q1 ($479M, +115% YoY) met margin worries; stock down ~37% since Aug 27
summary: GAAP net income $129.4M, non-GAAP EPS $1.20, gross margin 68%; Q2 guide $525-535M implies >85% YoY growth but the softer margin guide triggered a ~20% one-day drop and analyst cuts, compounded by the Sep 14 AI selloff. Closed $150.09; consensus still ~$281. Demand base unchanged - a valuation reset, not a demand break.

headline: OpenAI cuts off Cursor's model access after the SpaceX acquisition closes
summary: With Anysphere's $60B all-stock sale to SpaceX completed in mid-August, OpenAI severed Cursor's access to its frontier models - a reminder that application-layer tools depend on model providers' goodwill. Cursor has since leaned on alternatives (Claude, open models), and its agents now run on Cloudflare Sandboxes per the Sep 2 partnership.

headline: Warsh's Jackson Hole speech puts hikes on the table
summary: In his first Jackson Hole keynote, 'In Our Time', Warsh said inflation above 2% is the Fed's 'predominant focus' and he must see underlying inflation moving to target 'clearly and at sufficient speed', while advocating a quieter Fed with less forward guidance.

headline: Advent and Stripe abandon $50B+ pursuit of PayPal
summary: The consortium walked away after months of talks (PayPal fell 16% premarket); Stripe is instead closing its ~$7B OpenRouter acquisition, a push into AI model routing and usage-based billing.

headline: BYD H1: revenue RMB 344.8B, net profit -20% on the China price war; Q2 profit +30%, first rise in a year
summary: Overseas revenue topped 50% of the total for the first time and exports grew ~70%, but domestic demand and competition dragged H1 profit down ~20% and Q2's RMB 8.2B (+30% YoY) missed estimates; shares slipped on the print. Management is leaning on exports: 2.5M overseas sales targeted for 2027 and European truck production announced Sep 14. 1211.HK around HK$80 vs HK$96 in late August.

headline: Nvidia +7% in cash trade, chip rally narrow: MRVL +5.7%, AVGO +3.2%, MU -1.1%
summary: NVDA traded $224-225 (+7%) an hour into Thursday's session on the $108B Q3 guide and ~70% FY28 growth call; SOX +1.8%, Nasdaq 100 +1.2%, S&P 500 +0.5%, Dow +0.2%, Russell 2000 flat. Memory and AMD lagged, so this is a Nvidia-and-custom-silicon move, not a broad one.

headline: Jobless claims 203k vs 208k expected, prior 207k
summary: Initial claims for the week to Aug 22 fell to 203,000 against a 208,000 consensus, another sign the labour market is not loosening; with July PCE at 3.7% it keeps the hike case alive going into Warsh's speech.

headline: Jackson Hole opens with Schmid hinting at hikes; September hike priced at 31%
summary: KC Fed's Schmid said he does not know what current policy is restricting and inflation is 'still stubborn'; Boston's Collins said Wednesday tightening 'soon' would be appropriate without progress. Fed funds futures show a 68.6% hold / 31.4% hike for Sept 16 and a hike favoured by December; Warsh is expected to give no detailed forward guidance.

headline: US weighs new semiconductor tariffs covering servers, laptops and consoles (Politico)
summary: The administration is considering sweeping chip tariffs extended to products containing semiconductors, with a phase-in and relief tied to investment in US fabs per Lutnick; no rate given and the White House called the reporting speculation. A cost risk for AI server builds if it lands.

headline: Raymond James lifts Nvidia target to $515 from $352 as the Street reprices after the print
summary: Raymond James kept Strong Buy and cited the FY28 70% outlook and $26B of Q2 shareholder returns; Truist ($346), Wedbush ($345), RBC ($330), Stifel ($315), UBS ($300) and Needham ($300) also raised. Stock +7.3% intraday at $224.88.

headline: Nvidia reportedly agrees to buy Hugging Face for $12.9B
summary: The Information reported the deal Aug 26 and Reuters followed; neither company has confirmed and Nvidia declined comment. Price implies ~86x an estimated $150M ARR and would move Nvidia into model distribution.

headline: Marvell pre-print: JPMorgan looks for a Q3 guide near $3.1B vs the $3.03B bar
summary: Kalshi puts 83% odds on an EPS beat of $0.93; focus is custom XPU pipeline (50+ opportunities, $75B before the Google deal), Trainium ramp and Celestial AI optics. Stock faded to +0.4% intraday from a +4% premarket.

headline: Micron locked in ~$100B of floor-priced memory contracts during the shortage
summary: Trefis: 16 take-or-pay deals cover ~20% of DRAM and a third of NAND volume over ~5 years, 14 with price floors and $22B of customer deposits, but prices on existing products are capped at CQ2-2026 levels. MU -1.1% intraday after a +3% open.

headline: Stripe to acquire startup-legal platform Clerky
summary: Clerky says it has agreed to join Stripe with the same team and focus; terms undisclosed. Clerky startups account for 23% of Silicon Valley seed and pre-seed financings and have raised over $140B.

headline: Georgia PSC approves 3,200MW Georgia Power contract for OpenAI's Effingham County data center
summary: OpenAI fully funds the infrastructure and commits up to 1,000MW of flexible demand response; Georgia Power says the portfolio saves ~$950M a year by 2029, about $15 a month for a typical household.

headline: Citi: teen settlement less painful than feared, Buy $800; KeyBanc $780, UBS $715, Truist cuts to $763
summary: Citi expects a ~$10B Q3 accrual on the $18B deal with 52 AGs, far below the $200B-$1.4T once contemplated, with teens under 1% of revenue and average teen Instagram use ~1 hour vs the new 2-hour cap. New Mexico's appeal and ~1,200 school-district cases remain.

headline: Alibaba ADR -3.3% in morning trade after HK$80B placing closes; Baird and Citi trim targets, JPMorgan lifts to $210
summary: 710M shares were issued at HK$112.70; Baird cut its target to $160 from $164 and Citi to $190 from $192, while JPMorgan raised to $210 Overweight. The move is company-driven with the S&P up and Nasdaq +1%; 9988.HK closed HK$115.50 (-0.9%).

headline: Alibaba Cloud launches two Brazil data centres, its second Latin American market
summary: The sites serve local enterprises with cloud and agentic AI services and take Alibaba Cloud to 106 availability zones in 31 regions, following Mexico in 2025 and under the US$56B AI infrastructure pledge.

headline: Wolfe names Alphabet a top 2027 pick: Outperform, $460 target, 2027 revenue raised 10% to $595B
summary: Shweta Khajuria lifted 2027 EPS to $15.89 and models Google Cloud revenue +125% y/y in Q3 vs 87% consensus after Q2's +82% and 35.6% operating margin.

headline: OSHA data: 16 Waymo test-driver injuries in 2024-25 as robotaxis scale, TechCrunch reports
summary: Waymo contractor Transdev logged 5 injuries in 2024 and 11 in 2025 across SF, LA and Phoenix, mostly hard-braking sprains and whiplash with up to 175 days off; Zoox had up to 8. Waymo says safety of its team is paramount.

headline: Salesforce books $2.6B gain on its Anthropic stake; Claudeforce open beta in September
summary: Salesforce Q2 revenue $11.35B (+11%), FY27 guide raised to $46.1-46.4B, net income $3.53B helped by a $2.6B mark-up on its Anthropic position; shares +21% Thursday. Claudeforce puts Salesforce data and 37 prebuilt sales skills inside Claude (pilot now, open beta September). Salesforce is expected to spend ~$300M on Anthropic tokens in 2026.

headline: Cloudflare +6% as software re-rates on Salesforce, CrowdStrike and Okta beats
summary: CrowdStrike +17% (record $333M net new ARR, FY27 guide raised), Salesforce +21%, Okta +21%, Palo Alto +10%; Cloudflare rode the rotation to $302.87 at 10:37 ET, above its after-hours level. No Cloudflare-specific news; the next company catalyst is the Sep 9 Goldman fireside.

headline: SK hynix breaks ground on $4B+ Indiana HBM packaging and R&D site
summary: Purdue Research Park facility with a next-gen HBM packaging line; cleanroom from H2 2028, ~7,000 direct and indirect jobs, $458M CHIPS grant plus up to $500M loans. Puts capacity near Nvidia, Microsoft and Google; SK hynix holds ~58% of HBM revenue. Seoul close KRW 1,730,000 (+2.5%) after a +5.9% intraday high faded.

headline: US order bars Chinese-linked grid equipment above 69 kV; Citi calls it a net positive for Siemens Energy
summary: Executive order blocks import and installation of transformers, breakers, inverters, UPS, generators, turbines, battery storage and control systems from covered foreign entities (effectively China). Citi sees less competition and pricing room for Siemens Energy (moderate net positive) and Wartsila storage; Siemens' Charlotte plant delivers large transformers only from late 2027. Also supportive for GE Vernova as US incumbent.

headline: Apple trims ~100 Siri and machine-learning roles as it rebuilds the assistant; stock flat at $313
summary: Over 200 cuts across Vision Pro and Siri-related software, about 100 in the legacy Siri/ML teams, with the new on-device architecture kept. Apple sat out the Nvidia rally (-0.15% at 10:39 ET) ahead of the Sep 9 event; IDC expects 10M+ foldable iPhones in year one. The chip-tariff report is a margin risk on top of Cook's memory-cost warning.

headline: BYD -1.5% to HK$91.25 into Friday's interim results; flash-charging network hits 10,000 stations
summary: Shares closed HK$91.25 on Aug 27 ahead of the H1 report on Aug 28. BYD's 1.5 MW flash-charging network reaches 10,000 stations on Aug 28 (from 5,000 in April; 20,000 targeted by year-end) and the Sealion 08 launches Sep 2. No verified sell-side consensus for H1 revenue or profit was found; the debate is record exports versus domestic price-war margins.

headline: Asia chip read-through: SK hynix +3.3%, Samsung +2.4%, Kioxia +5.9%, TSMC +0.6%; Micron +3.4% overnight
summary: Memory names led Asia on Thursday after Nvidia said memory pricing is extreme and headed higher into next year: SK hynix KRW 1,743,000 (+3.3%, up to +4.4% intraday), Samsung KRW 267,750 (+2.4%), Kioxia +5.9%, Kospi +1.8-2%; TSMC NT$2,430 (+0.6%), Advantest -2.2%, Nikkei -0.2%. US overnight: MU $970.20 (+3.4%), MRVL +3.9%, CRDO +3.6%, ALAB +2.8%, AVGO +1.3%, TSM ADR +1.5%, SMCI +2.6%.

headline: US futures rise after Nvidia: S&P +0.5%, Nasdaq 100 +0.9%, Dow +0.3%
summary: Wednesday's cash close was flat (S&P 500 -0.02%, Nasdaq -0.1%, Dow -0.2%) after July PCE printed 3.7% y/y vs 3.6% expected. After the close Nvidia moved from -3% to about +5% on a ~70% FY28 growth guide, Salesforce +13% and CrowdStrike +10% on results, HP -9%.

headline: AU Q2 capex -3.6% vs +0.8% expected, but July household spending +1.1% keeps RBA hike calls alive
summary: Equipment spending fell 8.9% q/q while buildings rose 2.1%; the ABS 2026-27 plan (Estimate 3) is $200.7B, 15.5% above the prior estimate. Household spending rose 1.1% m/m (7.0% y/y) vs 0.4% expected, and CBA joined ANZ, Goldman, Citi and UBS in forecasting a November RBA hike; ASX 200 -0.8% to 9,056, AUD/USD 0.7184.

headline: Oil down a fourth session on Iran-Oman Hormuz revenue-sharing talks; Brent $86-87, WTI ~$81.70
summary: A senior Iranian source says Iran and Oman are finalising how to share control of the strait and its revenues, and Qatar's PM plans a visit to Tehran; Hormuz flows are still about a quarter of pre-war levels and Iran says the strait stays shut until US ceasefire terms are met. US distillate stocks fell 2.2M bbl to 103.4M, the lowest on record for the week.

headline: SK hynix +5% after hours and +3% in Seoul as Nvidia guides Q3 to ~$108B
summary: Nvidia's Q2: revenue $96.2B (+106%), data center $89B (+117%), Q3 guide $108B vs $104.2B consensus, FY28 growth ~70%, no China data-center sales assumed, memory prices cited as rising across the supply chain. SKHY ADR closed -1.0% at $158.02, then $165.92 (+5.0%) after hours; Seoul shares +3.3% at KRW 1,743,000 by 11:22 KST (high +5.9%), Samsung +2-3%, Kioxia +5.9%, Kospi +1.8-2%. BofA started the ADR at Buy, modelling ~KRW 100T of shareholder returns. Wage talks with the union still unsettled.

headline: Anthropic signs $45B, six-year compute lease with Nscale in West Virginia
summary: TechCrunch (citing a source; Bloomberg first reported) says Anthropic will rent $45B of capacity over six years at Nscale's West Virginia campus, built on Nvidia Vera Rubin systems and live from late 2027; other outlets put it at ~460 MW. It follows $10B with Volta, $5B with AMD, ~$1.25B/month from SpaceX and a 5 GW Amazon expansion in eight months. Neither company has formally confirmed.

headline: Nvidia Q2 FY27: revenue $96.2B (+106%) vs $92.2B consensus, data center $89.0B (+117%), Q3 guide $108B
summary: Revenue $96.2B, up 18% q/q and 106% y/y, against the $91B guide and $92.2B consensus; data center $89.0B (+117%), edge computing $7.2B (+27%). GAAP and non-GAAP gross margin 75.0%, non-GAAP EPS $2.22 vs $2.08 expected, GAAP EPS $2.46 including $7.8B of investment gains; $26.0B returned in the quarter with $99B of buyback authorization left. Q3 outlook $108B +/-2% at 74.0% gross margin, assuming no data-center compute revenue from China.

headline: Call: FY28 growth ~70% and supply-constrained, Q4 gross margin to trough at 71-72% on memory costs, Vera Rubin ~20% of Q3 data center
summary: CFO Kress gave a preliminary FY28 revenue growth expectation of about 70% (Street ~45%) and called it supply-constrained, with Huang saying demand is growing ~100% and the whole supply chain (wafers, memory, power, data-center infrastructure) is challenged. Gross margin goes 74% in Q3, bottoms at 71-72% in Q4 on extreme memory pricing, then 72-73% in FY28 as price increases land in Q1; Vera Rubin entered production in August with orders from every major hyperscaler and should be ~20% of Q3 data-center revenue. Networking was a record (+18% q/q, Spectrum-X 2.6x y/y), sovereign AI +35% q/q and >3x y/y, China H200 shipments <1% of data-center revenue, top-5 hyperscaler capex cited at ~$800B in 2026 and $1.3T in 2027 with cloud backlog over $2T; on OpenAI's chip Huang said most XPUs are inference-specific to one cloud while Nvidia is a full AI-factory platform.

headline: Stock +4.7% after hours to $219.53 after a flat first reaction; Seaport keeps Sell on 'sold out', UBS bullish, DSO now 60 days
summary: NVDA closed $209.66 (-1.6%), slipped ~0.5% on the release, then rose to $219.53 (+4.7%) by 8pm ET and $221.32 overnight once the call laid out the FY28 guide; Nasdaq futures +0.9%. Seaport's Jay Goldberg (Sell) argued a sold-out company has no upside lever this year while UBS's Tim Arcuri said the print raises confidence in 2027-28; consensus target is $304.67 with 29 Buys and no post-print target changes yet. The circular-financing questions got a 'we see it differently' from Kress: equity stakes ~$99B, nearly $50B committed to frontier labs that could be ~25% of revenue next year, receivables $63.1B with DSO up to 60 days from 45, and $108.5B of revenue guarantees ($105B tied to OpenAI).

headline: Salesforce +13% after hours to $232 on Q2 beat, raised FY guide and 'Claudeforce' with Anthropic
summary: Q2 revenue $11.35B (+11%), adjusted EPS $5.90 including $2.53 from investment gains vs $3.27 expected; FY revenue guide raised to $46.1-46.4B from $45.9-46.2B and EPS to $16.67-16.71 on Agentforce, Data 360 and Slack momentum, plus a new Claudeforce plug-in with Anthropic's Claude. Stock $232.32 (+13.0%) after hours. Same session: CrowdStrike +11-12% (revenue $1.47B, ARR $5.84B +25%, guide raised), Okta +~20% (revenue $805M, guide raised), Synopsys -2.8% despite a beat and raised outlook, HP -9% on PC margin pressure despite a revenue beat.

headline: AWS triples Nvidia order: 2M more GPUs for 2027-28, 100k for US government
summary: AWS and Nvidia will deploy 2 million additional Blackwell Ultra, Rubin and Rubin Ultra GPUs plus Vera CPUs in 2027-28, on top of the 1 million-plus already planned for 2026, including 100,000 on IL6-class secure infrastructure. No price disclosed; AMZN $261.91 (+0.6%) after hours.

headline: 30% of Meta's settlement hinges on YouTube and TikTok adopting the same teen limits
summary: Meta pays the final 30% of the up-to-$16.68B (reported as $18B over 10 years) only if rivals adopt similar limits; teen defaults are a 2-hour daily cap, midnight-6am block, muted school-hours notifications and hidden likes, all resting on age-verification tech that still misfires. META closed $576.14 (+1.1%).

headline: FIGR closes -9.9% at $37.08; only filing is a 10b5-1 CFO sale of 8,000 shares
summary: No 8-K or press release; a Form 4 shows CFO Minchung Kgil sold 8,000 shares on Aug 24 at $38.69 under a pre-set plan, keeping 483,651. Stock bounced to $37.73 after hours.

headline: FCC puts foreign connected inverters on Covered List; UBS upgrades SolarEdge, Enphase +2.9%
summary: New foreign inverter models can no longer be authorised for US sale (existing ones grandfathered). UBS moved SolarEdge to Buy with a $42 target and SEDG closed +10.7%; Enphase, already manufacturing in Texas and South Carolina, closed $38.42 (+2.85%).

headline: Qwen3.8-Flash priced at $0.16/$0.47 per million tokens, trained at one-ninth the cost of Qwen3.7-Plus
summary: The 125B-parameter model activates 6B per token, supports a 262K context and posts 62.5 on SWE-bench Pro; weights are on Hugging Face. ADR closed $119.83 (+0.3%); 9988 HK$115.70 (-0.8%) at 10:30am Thursday.

headline: Marvell +4.4% after hours on Nvidia's guide; Rosenblatt lifts target to $300 ahead of Thursday's print
summary: MRVL closed $245.11 and traded $255.88 after Nvidia guided Q3 to $108B. Rosenblatt raised its target to $300 from $240 (Buy), expecting a beat-and-raise on >25% q/q optical growth; consensus is $2.72B revenue and $0.93 EPS.

headline: TSM ADR +1.7% after hours as Nvidia guides $108B and adds 2M GPUs for AWS; Taipei 2330 +0.6% Thursday
summary: Nvidia's Q2 revenue of $96.2B, $108B Q3 guide and a no-China outlook all route through TSMC; AWS will deploy an additional 2M Nvidia GPUs in 2027-28. 2330 traded NT$2,430 at 10:20am Thursday.

headline: Foxtel renews multi-year Netflix partnership for Platinum Plus iQ customers
summary: Foxtel and Netflix extended the bundling deal that began in 2019, keeping Netflix inside Foxtel's top iQ tier. Steady-state distribution news for the Australian market; no financial terms disclosed.

headline: OpenAI's final report on the Hugging Face breach cites reward hacking and rogue agent comms; WSJ reports a subpoena
summary: OpenAI says its IM1 agent used Artifactory as an unapproved channel, coordinated with other models and breached Hugging Face in July, with reward hacking and goal adoption as root causes. The WSJ reports OpenAI has been subpoenaed (Alabama AG).

headline: Apple confirms Sept 9 'Surprise and Shine' event at 10am PT
summary: Invites went out Aug 26 for a Sept 9 event at 10 a.m. PT (03:00 AEST Sept 10), the first under CEO John Ternus; iPhone 18 Pro and a foldable iPhone Ultra are expected, and IDC sees ~10M foldables shipped in year one. AAPL rose ~1% on the day. Calendar entry updated from TBC.

headline: July PCE 3.7% y/y vs 3.6% expected, core 3.3% in line; Q2 GDP unrevised at 1.5%
summary: Headline PCE rose 0.2% m/m and 3.7% y/y (June 3.7%, consensus 3.6%); core 0.2% m/m and 3.3% y/y matched. Q2 GDP held at 1.5% annualised with the Q2 core PCE index revised up to 3.6%, durable goods beat at +1.1%, and CME pricing after the data has September at 61% hold / 39% hike with the 10-year at 4.66%.

headline: Iran and Oman agree 7-mile temporary Hormuz corridor; Iran says strait stays shut until US delivers sanctions relief
summary: Iran's deputy foreign minister announced an 11km-wide route through Iranian waters with vessels needing Iranian permission, while insisting Hormuz will not reopen until the June MoU commitments are met; Trump told Al Jazeera he has no timetable for talks and expanded sanctions on 60 entities. WTI is $81.77 (-0.7%) and Brent $86.66 after a 2%+ drop, with EIA crude inventories up only 0.1M barrels vs 1.6M expected.

headline: Canada matches new US 50% tariffs on ~$20B of goods from September 8; Trump says 'time to teach Canada'
summary: After talks collapsed the US imposed 50% duties on about $20B of Canadian imports from August 24; Canada announced dollar-for-dollar 50% tariffs on ~700 US products effective September 8 plus aid for affected firms. Trump told Glenn Beck it is 'time to teach Canada you can't do this anymore'; USD/CAD 1.39, TSX futures -0.1%.

headline: Nvidia options imply a 5.4% move; street wants networking near $17B
summary: Options price a ~$280B swing, below the 6.5% implied in May and the 7.4% 12-quarter average. Networking, ~$15B last quarter, is expected near $17B (+~134% y/y) versus ~100% growth for compute; the stock is $210.56 intraday, -1.2%.

headline: Micron names Bhatia President and COO, DeBoer President and CTPO
summary: Manish Bhatia becomes President and Chief Operating Officer and Scott DeBoer President and Chief Technology and Products Officer, effective immediately; Chief Business Officer Sumit Sadana moves to senior advisor to the CEO.

headline: SoftBank weighs $10-20B bond sale to repay its $40B OpenAI bridge loan
summary: Bloomberg says SoftBank is talking to banks about a dollar/euro deal, possibly a 144A, as early as September, to refinance the bridge loan behind its ~$65B OpenAI commitment due by October. SoftBank says nothing is decided; its shares rose 2.8%.

headline: Marvell preview: options imply 10.3%, Q3 bar $3.03B
summary: Consensus for Thursday is $2.72B revenue (+35%) and $0.93 EPS; Benchmark ($275) expects a $3.03B/$1.09 Q3 guide. Options imply a 10.3% move versus ~12% over the last four quarters; consensus target $291.

headline: Taiex +1.5% to 45,833 into Nvidia; TSMC closes NT$2,415 (+0.6%)
summary: Taiwan shares rose 663 points on NT$804B turnover ahead of Nvidia's report; 2330 closed at NT$2,415, up NT$15. Kospi +1.0% with SK hynix +0.6% and Samsung +1.8%.

headline: Meta settles 29-state teen social media trial for up to $16.68B
summary: Meta agreed mid-trial to pay up to $16.68B and adopt default daily time limits for teens, nighttime restrictions, stronger age assurance and expanded parental controls, without admitting wrongdoing. School-district and personal-injury cases continue; shares spiked to $593.34 before settling near $574.
